newsitem.title: USA: Isis says '2302' has positive test results.
newsitem.headline: Isis says '2302' has positive test results.

text.p: Isis Pharmaceuticals said that its ISIS 2302, an antisense anti-inflammatory drug, demonstrated safety and efficacy in a Phase II study of patients with Crohn's disease.
The positive results of the study is the first evidence of therapeutic benefit with a syustematically administered antisense drug, it said. Crohn's disease is a form of inflammatory bowel disease.
The results form the basis for the decision by ISIS and its partner, Boehringer Ingelheim of Germany, to proceed with the full-scale development of ISIS 2302, it said.
Isis said that in the randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled study, 47 percent of patients treated with the drug showed remission versus none in the placebo group after a month of treatment.

The mean duration of the remission in the responding patients was prolonged, lasting almost five months following a single course of treatment, it said. A statistifcally significant lowering of corticosteriod requirements was achieved in the group tested with the drug from the first month through the end of the study at six months, it said.

Daniel Kisner, president and chief oeprating officer of Isis, said data from the study show that the drug can induce high levels of response and disease remission and that patients can be weaned from dependency on steroids, one of the disease's current treatments.
"We are eager to initiate a pivotal quality study of ISIS 2302 in Crohn's disease within the next one or two months," he said.

The information from the study, which was inadvertently released by Reuters, was provided in a press release, embargoed until 0500 EST/1000 GMT Friday. The study was to be announced at the Canadian Digestive Disease Week Conference at 1030 EST Friday in Quebec City.
